memos.headline: MSFT and NVDA Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; AAPL and UNH Remain Broken
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market within our universe. MSFT is trading within 0.8% of its 52-week high, +11.6% above its 50-day and +13.2% above its 200-day mean, with 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +17.2%—this is the cleanest uptrend in the group, though RSI at 71.5 warns of near-term overbought risk. NVDA shows a similar profile: +16.6% above its 50-day, +11.2% above its 200-day, and 12-week rel strength of +15.5%, with RSI at a more comfortable 62.7. On the other side, AAPL is deeply impaired—24.2% off its high, 12.5% below its 200-day mean, and bleeding relative strength at -14.0% over 12 weeks; I would need a reclaim of the 200-day (roughly $224) to reconsider. UNH is in a structural downtrend, nearly 50% off its high and 38% below its 200-day, and while the 4-week bounce of +14.3% is notable, the damage is too severe to trust—I'd need a sustained move above the 50-day (roughly $390) before engaging. PG is quietly deteriorating with negative relative strength and RSI at 40.3, offering no reason to own it here.

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe, near 52-week highs with +17.2% 12-week rel strength vs SPY; would reassess on a close below the 50-day (~$425).
Robust uptrend with +20.8% 12-week return and +15.5% rel strength; RSI 62.7 leaves room to run, but a break below $122 (200-day area) would negate.
Trading 12.5% below its 200-day mean with -14.0% 12-week rel strength and RSI 40.7; trend is decisively down until price reclaims ~$224.
Nearly 50% off its high and 38% below the 200-day; the 4-week bounce is a bear-market rally until proven otherwise—need a close above ~$390.
Decent 4-week rel strength of +5.4% and above both moving averages, but 12-week rel strength is only +1.3% and still 15% off highs—moderate conviction; invalidated below $162.
Below both the 50-day and 200-day means with RSI 40.3 and -10.2% 12-week rel strength; no technical reason to own.
Healthy longer-term trend (+9.6% above 200-day) but 4-week rel strength has turned negative at -2.1%; watching $251 (200-day area) as support.
Above both averages with RSI 59.9 but still 12.4% off highs and only modest rel strength; needs to clear $242 to turn fully constructive.
Strong 1-week bounce of +7.5% pushed RSI to 68.7, but 12-week rel strength is -8.1% and price is flat vs the 200-day; could be a short-term mean-reversion pop.
Recovering toward the 50-day with +9.6% premium but still flat vs the 200-day and 14.4% off highs; trend is ambiguous until a break above $417.

memos.headline: Mega-cap tech earnings power dominates; CAT and XOM face margin compression
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in MSFT, NVDA, and GOOGL, all posting double-digit revenue growth with net margins north of 36%. MSFT delivered $70.07B in revenue (+13.3% YoY) with a 36.9% net margin and manageable $42.88B total debt, while NVDA's 69.2% YoY revenue surge to $44.06B at a 42.6% net margin on only $8.46B of debt is extraordinary. GOOGL printed $90.23B in revenue (+12.0% YoY) with a 38.3% net margin and just $14.79B in debt—the cleanest balance sheet relative to earnings in this universe. On the other end, CAT's revenue fell 9.8% YoY to $14.25B with net income down 29.8%, and XOM's net income declined 6.2% on essentially flat revenue, signaling cyclical headwinds I'm unwilling to pay through. The line items that would change my view are any sustained margin compression at NVDA (currently 42.6%) or a reacceleration in CAT's top line above mid-single digits.

views.note: 13.3% revenue growth, 36.9% net margin, and 17.7% net income growth on moderate leverage make this the most reliable compounder in the universe.
69.2% YoY revenue growth to $44.06B with a 42.6% net margin and only $8.46B debt is exceptional, though I discount slightly for cyclicality risk in AI capex.
38.3% net margin on $90.23B revenue with 46% net income growth and minimal debt gives the best margin-of-safety profile here.
Net income surged 64.2% YoY to $17.13B as margins expanded to 11.0%, but $58.75B in debt and still-thin margins relative to peers temper my conviction.
Revenue grew only 5.1% YoY to $95.36B with $92.20B in total debt—the highest in the tech group—and net income growth of 4.8% is pedestrian for the valuation.
Solid 32.3% net margin and 9.1% net income growth, but $407B total debt and macro sensitivity keep me from taking a directional view.
Revenue declined 2.1% YoY to $19.78B with net income essentially flat; I need to see organic growth reaccelerate before getting constructive.
Revenue grew 9.8% to $109.58B but the 5.7% net margin is the thinnest in the universe and YoY net income comparison is unavailable, limiting visibility.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% YoY to $2.00B signals clear cyclical deterioration; I refuse to pay for compressing cash flow.
Flat revenue and a 6.2% decline in net income to $7.71B on $32.82B of debt point to commodity-driven margin erosion with no near-term catalyst.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Benign CPI and Softening Labor Market — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Neutral Banks
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in a pause regime: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, CPI is running at just 2.3% y/y, and unemployment has drifted up 40bp over the past year to 4.3%. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+90bp y/y to +0.46pp), consistent with the market pricing eventual easing while the front end stays anchored. The 10y yield at 4.41% is only modestly higher over three months (+14bp), suggesting the long end is comfortable with the inflation trajectory. This backdrop — cooling labor market, contained inflation, positive curve slope — favors duration-sensitive growth equities and is broadly neutral for banks and cyclicals. A surprise jump in core CPI above 3% or a payroll print pushing unemployment below 4.0% would flip my regime call back toward hawkish risk-off.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap benefits from a pause-to-easing trajectory with 2.3% CPI and a steepening curve.
Same duration tailwind as AAPL; stable rates and benign inflation support growth multiples.
Growth-duration play benefits from rate pause, though elevated 10y at 4.41% caps multiple expansion somewhat.
Consumer-facing cyclical growth name aided by cooling inflation and eventual easing expectations.
Steeper curve (+90bp y/y in 10y-2y) helps NIM, but rising unemployment at 4.3% raises credit-loss risk — offsetting forces.
Macro regime is mildly softening with unemployment rising; energy demand outlook is uncertain, keeping me sidelined.
Staples are a natural hedge in slowdowns, but with CPI at 2.3% and no recession signal yet, there is no urgency to overweight defensives.
Cyclical bellwether faces headwinds from softening labor market (+0.4pp y/y unemployment) but no outright contraction signal yet.
Defensive healthcare name is macro-insensitive; no strong macro tilt in either direction at current data.
Ad-driven growth benefits from contained inflation and a pause regime that supports risk appetite and multiples.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: MSFT and NVDA Positive Momentum vs. UNH Leadership Churn Warning
memos.body: I see a clear split in narrative tone across the universe as of mid-June. MSFT's +7.6% earnings-day pop on 4/30 was the strongest single-day reaction in the group and signals genuinely positive sentiment that may still have legs given the absence of negative follow-on filings. NVDA's +3.2% post-earnings move on 5/28 confirms the AI demand narrative remains intact, though the positive tone is becoming crowded. On the negative side, UNH has filed four separate Departure/Appointment of Directors or Officers 8-Ks between late April and early June—an unusually high cadence of leadership turnover that I read as a deteriorating internal narrative likely not yet fully priced. AAPL's -3.7% earnings reaction and PG's -3.7% earnings drop both suggest cautious-to-negative sentiment, though PG's active conference-circuit engagement (Deutsche Bank presentation 6/5, Arnold announcement 6/9) hints at management trying to stabilize the narrative.

views.note: Strongest earnings-day price reaction in the universe at +7.6% with no subsequent negative filings suggests positive sentiment has room to run.
+3.2% post-earnings pop confirms AI demand narrative but crowded positive tone limits further upside from sentiment alone.
Four director/officer departure filings in six weeks signals unusual leadership instability that typically precedes further negative narrative shifts.
The -3.7% earnings reaction on 5/1 set a negative tone and the subsequent 'Other Events' filing on 5/12 did not provide a clear positive catalyst to reverse it.
Earnings-day -3.7% drop was negative but active management engagement at Deutsche Bank and the Arnold announcement suggest an effort to stabilize sentiment.
+1.7% earnings reaction and high filing cadence (five 8-Ks since mid-April) indicate steady positive engagement without signs of narrative fatigue.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and routine subsequent filings suggest no strong sentiment signal in either direction.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing From Peaks but Structurally Elevated; Supply-Chain and China Exposure Remain Key Differentiators
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 484.65 has dropped 27% over the past month but remains nearly 12% above its level three months ago, signaling that while the acute tariff/trade-policy shock is fading, the structural policy backdrop is still unsettled. VIX at 18.02 (down 26% over 3 months) and HY OAS at 3.17% confirm markets are pricing a calmer near-term, but I would not extrapolate this into a durable all-clear for names with heavy China/export-control exposure. WTI at $68.73 (+8.5% m/m) suggests some demand recovery or supply tightening, which is modestly supportive for energy but also raises input-cost risk for industrials and consumer staples. My highest-conviction geopolitical call is to remain cautious on NVDA and AAPL given ongoing semiconductor export-control risk and China assembly concentration, while I favor JPM and XOM as relatively insulated from the trade-policy overhang. A material escalation in US-China semiconductor restrictions or a new round of tariffs on consumer electronics would sharpen these views.

views.note: Semiconductor export controls to China remain the single largest geopolitical tail risk for this name; elevated but declining policy uncertainty does not resolve the structural overhang.

China assembly concentration and potential consumer-electronics tariff exposure keep me from going long despite the easing in headline uncertainty; the 8-K on 5/12 offers no clarity on supply-chain shifts.
Financials are relatively insulated from trade-policy friction; a steepening 10y-2y spread (+15bp over 3m) and tight HY OAS support the earnings outlook.
WTI at $68.73 with an 8.5% monthly bounce and limited direct exposure to China policy risk make XOM a reasonable geopolitical hedge in the current environment.
Three 8-Ks in six weeks suggest active investor communication, likely around tariff-driven cost pressures; I stay neutral until I see clearer margin guidance amid still-elevated policy uncertainty.
Frequent Reg FD filings (four since late April) hint at proactive guidance management around input costs and FX; geopolitical risk is moderate but rising commodity prices could pressure margins.

Maintain moderate positions in AMZN and JPM where analyst views are mixed but net constructive, and hold meaningful cash given overbought signals in the leaders and residual geopolitical uncertainty.

RSI at 71.5 is the only caution, warranting a tight stop.
